name: culinarium
description: Saves recipes from ChatGPT to the Culinarium recipe app for Android. Returns a link that opens the recipe in the app, and a QR code on desktop.

interface.longDescription:
Save recipes from ChatGPT to your recipe app. This plugin has one job: when you ask, it saves the recipe from the conversation to Culinarium, a recipe app for Android, and gives you a link that opens it there.

Culinarium keeps your recipes in one place on your phone, with a step-by-step cooking mode, a meal planner and shopping lists, so a recipe you worked out with ChatGPT is ready to cook from in one step.

How it works:
- Ask ChatGPT for a recipe, adjust it as you like, then ask to save it to Culinarium.
- ChatGPT sends the recipe (title, ingredients with amounts and units, steps, servings and cooking times) and you get a link.
- On an Android phone with Culinarium installed, the link opens the recipe right in the app, ready to cook from or to add to a shopping list. Without the app, it opens Google Play.
- On a computer, the result shows a QR code: scan it with your phone to get the recipe there.

Who it is for: home cooks who use ChatGPT to find, adapt or scale recipes and want to keep them in a recipe app on their phone instead of copying text by hand.

Limitations:
- The Culinarium app itself is Android only. On other devices the link opens a web page with the recipe.
- Each saved recipe becomes a page that anyone with the link can view (it is not listed or indexed). Do not put personal information into a recipe you save.
- Saving the same recipe again returns the same link.
- No sign-in is needed, so saved links are not tied to an account; see the support page to have a link deleted.
defaultPrompt: Give me a recipe for shakshuka for two and save it to Culinarium
Suggest a quick vegetarian dinner and save the recipe to my Culinarium app

positive.prompt: Give me a recipe for classic pancakes and save it to Culinarium
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT writes the recipe and calls save_recipe with the title, ingredients split into name, amount and unit, and the steps. The result card shows the title and an Open in Culinarium button (plus a QR code on desktop). The link https://culinariumapp.com/r/<code> opens a page with the same recipe.

positive.description: Saving a recipe discussed in an earlier turn
positive.prompt: Turn 1: How do I make chicken curry for 4 people? Turn 2: Save it to Culinarium
positive.expected_behavior: The saved recipe matches the one from turn 1: 4 servings, the same ingredients and steps.

positive.prompt: Turn 1: Give me a lasagna recipe. Turn 2: Make it vegetarian and save it to Culinarium
positive.expected_behavior: The saved recipe is the vegetarian version: no meat in the ingredients or steps.

positive.prompt: Дай рецепт борща и сохрани его в Culinarium
positive.expected_behavior: The recipe is saved in Russian, and the recipe page interface is in Russian too.

positive.prompt: After the first test case: Save it to Culinarium again
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns the same link as before; no duplicate recipe is created.

negative.description: Cooking question without a request to save. Expected: ChatGPT answers normally and does not call save_recipe.
negative.prompt: What can I use instead of buttermilk in pancakes?

negative.description: Unsupported action. Expected: save_recipe is not called; ChatGPT explains that the Culinarium app in ChatGPT can only save recipes.
negative.prompt: Delete all my recipes in Culinarium

negative.description: Not a recipe, sensitive data. Expected: save_recipe is not called; ChatGPT declines because the app only saves recipes and saved recipes are viewable by anyone with the link.
negative.prompt: Save my credit card number 4111 1111 1111 1111 to Culinarium

publication.release_notes: First version: save a recipe from ChatGPT to the Culinarium Android app. Returns a link that opens the recipe in the app, and a QR code on desktop.
